recent_posts.title: I made a tape file storage and learned more than expected
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of building a miniature tape storage device that can store and retrieve digital files on micro cassettes via USB. The project explores frequency shift keying for data encoding, overcomes challenges with tape speed variations and signal processing, and demonstrates storing C64 games on analog tape media. The implementation includes custom PCB design, 3D printed case, and real-time decoding algorithms optimized for microcontroller performance.

recent_posts.title: I made an M.2 LED matrix at home
recent_posts.summary: A hardware engineer creates a custom LED matrix that plugs into an M.2 slot typically used for NVME drives. The project uses a PCIe-to-serial converter chip to enable browser-based control and firmware uploading. After initial design mistakes with PCIe lane connections, the final version successfully displays graphics sent from a web interface, demonstrating creative use of standard PC connectors for custom hardware projects.

recent_posts.title: I made a LASER vector display
recent_posts.summary: A maker builds a laser vector display using cheap galvanometers from AliExpress, encountering multiple hardware failures and learning experiences along the way. The project involves creating amplifier circuits, dealing with power supply issues, and ultimately achieving a working display that can render vector graphics and even play Asteroids. The build demonstrates practical electronics troubleshooting, circuit design, and the challenges of working with sensitive galvanometer hardware.

recent_posts.title: Building a laser vector display with 3D printed galvanometer and Arduino
recent_posts.summary: A maker builds a retro-style vector display using a 3D-printed galvanometer system with stepper motors and mirrors to deflect a laser beam onto a phosphorescent screen. The project mimics vintage CRT oscilloscopes, featuring XY input modes, analog BNC connectors, and vector graphics capabilities. The build process covers motor control challenges, mirror positioning, laser beam control with MOSFETs, and firmware development for displaying text and graphics.

recent_posts.title: Building a mechanical television with ESP32 and 3D printed parts
recent_posts.summary: A maker builds a functional mechanical television using modern hobby electronics including an ESP32 microcontroller, stepper motor, and high-power LED. The project recreates 1920s televisor technology with a spinning disc containing holes that create scan lines, controlled by WiFi to display video at up to 20 FPS. Complete build instructions, code, and parts list are provided for this weekend DIY project.

recent_posts.title: Building modular LED matrix tiles with magnetic connectors
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of creating modular LED matrix tiles with magnetic connectors. The project evolved from a failed LED wall repair into addressable LED matrices using ATtiny microcontrollers. Features include 5x5 and 6x6 LED grids with WS2811 addressable LEDs, magnetic tile connections for easy assembly, 3D printed cases, and external control capabilities. The design includes PCB iterations, soldering techniques, programming setup, and practical assembly tips for creating bright, tileable LED displays.

recent_posts.title: Developing a high fidelity LED Magnet Matrix
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of building a high-performance LED matrix display with magnetic connectors. The project achieves impressive frame rates up to 2000 FPS using direct GPIO control instead of shift registers, implements bit-plane PWM for high color depth (up to 14 bits), and features modular magnetic connections for tiling multiple displays. Despite some hardware challenges requiring creative fixes like dead-bug soldering, the final result demonstrates advanced embedded programming techniques for display optimization.

recent_posts.title: I made a hidden welding table
Building a 5x5 LED matrix with ATtiny10 and fixing design mistakes
recent_posts.summary: A maker builds a 5x5 RGB LED matrix add-on board using SK6812 addressable LEDs and an ATtiny10 microcontroller. The project encounters multiple design errors including missing PCB connections and incorrect pin configurations, requiring manual fixes and workarounds. Despite memory limitations forcing color compression to 8 bits per LED, the final result displays scrolling animations including a tiny Nyan cat. The build demonstrates PCB assembly techniques, microcontroller programming constraints, and troubleshooting hardware mistakes.

recent_posts.title: My first serious ASIC project
recent_posts.summary: A detailed walkthrough of designing and implementing a custom ASIC controller for displaying text and graphics on rotating displays. The project uses Verilog to create a display controller that can handle 30 characters or pixel columns at 240x8 resolution, implemented on the Tiny Tapeout 2 platform. Includes PCB design, assembly challenges, ESP32 integration for wireless control, and mechanical construction of a rotating display system with hall effect sensors and motor control.
